content:
Apple has filed for a preliminary injunction in its ongoing trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI. Apple says it would suffer "irreparable harm" from the alleged theft of trade secrets if the injunction is not granted.

In its filing, Apple says it wrote to OpenAI after filing its initial lawsuit last month, expressing an intent to "seek injunctive preliminary relief." However, Apple says it would not pursue such legal action if OpenAI agreed to five requests:

  • Stop accessing or using Apple's confidential information
  • Stop any ongoing use or disclosure
  • Preserve all evidence
  • Allow forensic inspection of devices, cloud storage, email, Slack, Teams, and other repositories
  • Search OpenAI's systems for any Apple confidential information

Apple says OpenAI has agreed to the first three requests, but the two parties have not reached agreement on the final two.

As a result, Apple is asking the court to issue a preliminary injunction that would order a judge to immediately bar OpenAI from using or obtaining any Apple trade secrets, preserve all evidence, allow Apple to conduct forensic inspections of OpenAI's devices and accounts, and return any Apple confidential information still in OpenAI's possession.

Apple says:

Apple has separately filed a motion asking the court to expedite discovery, including the early production of documents and out-of-court depositions of key OpenAI employees and management.

Alongside Apple's filing, OpenAI published its longest public response yet to Apple's lawsuit. In a blog post published late at night, OpenAI said the "reckless, belligerent, and unusually personal" lawsuit does not befit Apple's reputation as "one of the greatest companies in history."

A hearing on the injunction is scheduled for October 1, 2026. You can view the full filing below.
